title: Xerxes' Road to Salamis
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Step through ten places of the Persian Wars on a map, from Sardis and Marathon to Thermopylae, Salamis and Mycale, and infer at five of them why the fighting or the crossing happened there.

learningObjectives: Infer, at five places in the Persian Wars, why the fighting or the crossing happened there, choosing the geographic reason before it is revealed and getting at least 4 of 5 correct.

keyQuestions: Why did the Persians land at Marathon?
Why did Xerxes cross the Hellespont at Abydos?
Why did the Greeks try to stop the army at Thermopylae?
Why did the Persians find Athens almost empty?
Why did Themistocles want to fight in the strait of Salamis?
commonMisconceptions: The Greeks won because they had more soldiers or ships.
The Persian army and fleet traveled separately and did not depend on each other.
The Athenians defended their city walls in 480 BCE.
The Persian Wars were one battle at Marathon.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on five prediction questions (mastery: 4 of 5).
Explain why narrow places favored the smaller Greek forces.
